chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He (peace be upon him) asked me: 'Does Ibn Abi Layth judge with a judgment and then retract from it?' So I said to him: 'It has reached me that he judged regarding the chattels of the man and the woman when one of them died, so the heirs of the living and the heirs of the deceased claimed it, or the man divorced her, so the man claimed it and the women claimed it. He judged with four judgments.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what was that?' So I said: 'As for the first of them, he judged in it by the saying of Ibrahim al-Nakhai': he made the chattels of the woman which were not suitable for men to be for the woman, and the chattels of the man which were not suitable for women to be for the man, and whatever was for men and women, he divided it between them in two halves.'

Then it reached me that he said: 'They are both claimants together, so that which is in their hands entirely, he divided between them in two halves.' Then he said: 'The man is the owner of the house, and the woman is the one entering upon him, and she is the claimant, so all the chattels are for the man except the chattels of the women which do not belong to men, so these are for the woman.'

Then he judged after that with a judgment, had I not witnessed it, I would not have referred it to him. A woman from us died, and she had a husband, and she left chattels. So we raised the matter to him, so he said: 'Write down the chattels.' So when he read it, he said to the husband: 'This which is for the man and the woman, we have made it for the woman, except for the scale, for it is from the chattels of the man, so it is for you.'

So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'So upon what is he today?' I said: 'He has reverted to what was said by the saying of Ibrahim al-Nakhai': that he made the house for the man.' Then I asked him about that, so I said to him: 'What do you say about it?' So he said: 'The saying which you informed me that you witnessed, even though he had reverted from it.'

So I said: 'The chattels are for the woman?' So he said: 'What is your view if she establishes proof, how much would she need?' I said: 'Two witnesses.' So he said: 'If you were to ask the ones between the two mountains, and we are at that time in Makkah, they would tell you that the dowry and the chattels are gifted openly from the house of the woman to the house of her husband, so she is the one who brought it. And this claimant, if he claims that he has added anything to it, let him bring proof upon it.'
ai.seo_question: How did the judge Ibn Abi Layth rule on the division of household property between husband and wife according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* (Chapter 27) documents the jurisprudential evolution of the judge Ibn Abi Layth regarding household chattels (*matā'*), reflecting the dynamic nature of *fiqh* through his shifting rulings. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual evidence, particularly the custom of wives openly gifting items to the marital home, which shifts the burden of proof to the husband if he claims ownership of specific additions. This narrative underscores the practical application of legal reasoning (*ijtihad*) within the early Shia community in Mecca.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> asked me: ‘Has Ibn Abu Layli ever judged with a judgement, then retracted from it?’

So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘It has reached me that he judged with regards to the chattels (possessions) of the man and the woman, when one of the two had died, so the inheritors of the alive and the inheritors of the deceased claimed it, or the man divorced her, so the man claimed it and the women claimed it. He judged with four judgements’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what was that?’

So I said, ‘As for the first one of these, so he judged in it by the worlds of Ibrahim Al-Nakhai’e who had made the possessions of the woman which were not correct for the men, to be for the women, and the chattels of the man which were not correct for the women, to be for the men, and whatever was for the men and the women, (to be divided) between the two of them in two halves.

Then it reached me that he said, ‘They are both together claimants, so that which is their hands entirely, (to be divided) between the two of them by two halves’. Then he said, ‘The man is the owner of the house, and the woman is the coming upon him as an outsider, and she is the claimant, so the chattels, all of them are for the man except for the chattels of the woman which cannot happen to be for the men, so these are for the woman’.

Then he judged after that with such a judgement, had I not witnessed it, I would not have referred it to him. A woman from us died, and for her was her husband, and she left chattels. So we raised the matter to him, so he said, ‘Write down the (list of) chattels’. So when he read it, he said to the husband, ‘This which happens to be for the man and the woman, so we make it to be for the woman, except for the scale, for it is from a chattels of the man, so it is for you’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘So upon which thing is he on today?’ I said, ‘He has reverted to what was said by the words of Ibrahim Al-Nakhai’e that the house is to be made to be for the man’. Then I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about that, so I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying with regards to it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The words which you informed me<sup>asws</sup> that you witnessed it, even though he had reverted from it’.

So I said, ‘The chattels (possessons) happen to be for the woman?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘What is your view that if she had to establish proof, how much would she need to?’ So I said, ‘Two witnesses’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you were to ask the ones between the two mountains, and we are today at Makkah, they would tell you that the baggage and the chattels which were gifted openly from the house of the woman to the house of her husband, so these are which she came with, and if he were to claim, so if he claims that he has renewed any of these, so it is upon him to establish the proof’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has narrated the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked me, ‘Does ibn abu Layla 5 reverse his judgments? 5 I replied, ‘I have come to know that he issued a judgment about the assets of man and woman when one of them died and the living heirs claim it as well as the heirs of the dead, or when she is divorced then the men claim it as well as women. It is about four cases.

He (the Imam) asked, ‘What are they? 5 I replied, ‘The first is that he issued judgment by the words of Ibrahim al-Nakha‘iy. He (Ibrahim) would give the items that were especially for women to women and those for men to men and whatever was for both men and women, divide between them half-and-half.
Then I came to know that he said, “Men are the owner of the house and women are additions on them. She is the plaintiff. All items belong to men except those especially for women which are for women.

55 He then issued a judgment that if I had not experienced it I would not mention. A woman from us died and left behind her husband and assets. I took the case before him. He then asked us to list the goods. When he read it, he then said to the husband, “This is for both man and woman so we give it to the woman, except the balance because it is of the assets of man and it is for you.

55 5 He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is his judgment now? 5 I replied, ‘He has reversed and now he says according to the words of Ibrahim al-Nakha‘iy that the house is for man. 5 I then asked him (the Imam) what he (the Imam) said in the case. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the case that you experienced and that he then reversed.

5 1 then asked, ‘Do the items belong to the woman? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Consider, if she were to present proof; how much proof would she need? 5 1 replied, ‘She needed two witnesses. 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Were you to ask from between the two mountains - we were in Makkah in those days - they tell you that the items and assets that are given as gifts publicly from the house of the woman to the house of her husband is what she has brought (belongs to her). He is the plaintiff and if he thinks that he has increased anything to it he must present testimony.
